answer: A spice-desk seat needs a one-use crocus assay. The applicant locks 31 coins and draws a clerk-sealed 0.42 g saffron lot whose four crocin HPLC peaks are posted at issue. In 17 minutes they cure the threads over a licensed juniper brazier whose smoke-VOC hash already sits on-ledger, then press the cooled filaments onto an 8-cm numbered lotus-leaf platen. Peers require mass within 0.9 mg, all four peaks within 0.3 min retention, and the platen serial in frame. A dyed substitute or borrowed brazier misses the VOC hash, the stake burns, and one kitchen cannot mint a crowd of aliases.
